_source.displaydescription:
Dathu Bāhāḥ is a member of the branch of Mayūravarṇa Mahāvihāra and is situated southwest of this monument. It is one of three bāhāḥs that are located near to the Mayūravarṇa Mahāvihāra at its southeast corner. Dathu is positioned in between these, which is how it gained its name. The Bāhāḥ can be accessed through an underpass underneath a residential building from the western Cidhaṃ Bāhāḥ (LAL2070). This Bāhāḥ has been built on the eastern wing and faces west. At present, however, it consists only of a ground floor, and this is also in ruins.

Before 2015, this site was a three-storey Bāhāḥ complex. Three plain windows were installed on its first floor, and a secret room was located on this level. The second floor contained a trikhājhyāḥ flanked by two plain windows. The roof of the Bāhāḥwas made from zinc sheets. However, the first and second floors collapsed during the 2015 earthquake. Although the ground floor was badly damaged, the sanctum of the Bāhāḥ has remained safe.

The ground floor has three colonnaded bays on its main facade; the central bay holds the main door. The space between the columns on the right-hand side is filled with brick masonry, while a small entry way can be found on the left. The architecture shows that this Bāhāḥ has stood witness to different periods of time. The main door is well carved and once was surmounted by a ṭoraṇa thã held up by stone lions, however the ṭoraṇa was removed after the earthquake. Historical photos show that the first and second floor contained a single opening window and a triple-bay window (svapājhyaḥ) respectively. The back wall (to the east) has been heavily damaged and parts of it have collapsed. The main sanctum room has been covered with CGI sheets to protect it from rain. The courtyard (8.95m x 7.25m) is paved in telia tiles, and contains a Dharmadhātu Maṇḍala and a Śikharakūṭa Caitya (160cm high) lined up in the central axis in front of the main sanctum (to the west). The courtyard is still filled with debris from the collapsed building materials.

Inside the sanctum, the stone statue of the seated main deity, Akṣobhya Buddha, faces west. The original statue was stolen some time between 1983-1985. Later, a similar statue was enshrined and covered with a metal garment. After the 2015 earthquakes, however, the metal garment of the deity disappeared. A small stone Caitya and a stone with sculpted images of four donors has also been preserved inside the sanctum. Before the earthquake, there was also a wooden toraṇa dated NS 1004 with an image of Akṣobhya in the middle, Prajñāpāramitā on the right and Ṣaḍakṣarī Lokeśvara on the left (Locke 1985, 87). After the earthquake, broken pieces of the toraṇa were found scattered around, but the piece containing the date could not be located. The pinnacle which was once fixed on top of the toraṇa can now be seen above the entrance. Images of Hanumān and Mahākāla also survived the earthquake; they are now placed to the north and the south of the entrance.
